solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To have houses bloody demolished

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
blood is red
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: Someone's houses are being knocked down, and they are cursing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: TO and OWN together house RED: TO(RED)OWN. 'Bloody' reads as a mild British swear word but supplies the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore down is the past tense of the phrasal verb meaning to knock a building flat.

clue.text: Reducing volume, record band

blocks.note: to tape something is to record it
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A sound engineer turns down the volume while recording a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians beside 'record', but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapering narrows gradually, so its bulk or size diminishes towards one end.

clue.text: It might make a drunk driver pensive

blocks.note: rum in someone is what might make them drunk
the driver ant is an African army ant

explanation.surface: A warning that drink could turn a motorist thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RUM IN ANT: rum inside a driver ant would make it drunk. The motorist in the surface is really an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant, as an adjective, describes someone chewing things over in thought, meditative.

clue.text: Slow speech from medic — it's boring

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A doctor's slow, dull way of talking puts the listener to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means tedious in the surface but drilling holes in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy, drawn-out manner of speaking with prolonged vowels.

clue.text: Trump imitator usually seated?

blocks.note: surface reading: an impersonator of a certain politician sitting down
setter's reading: trump is British slang for breaking wind, and this joke-shop item mimics that noise when sat on

explanation.surface: An impressionist who does a famous president, usually from a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain to trump is to fart; the novelty rubber bag makes the sound when someone sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank toy, an inflatable bladder placed on a chair, imitates a rude noise under the person sitting.

clue.text: Fighting depression will not finish artist

indicators.note: a word that does not finish loses its final letter

blocks.note: war is fighting
a hole is a depression in the ground, here missing its end

explanation.surface: An artist suffering from combat-induced depression may never complete a work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like the mental state but is a dip in the ground, HOLE cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist famous for soup-can and celebrity prints.

clue.text: Stars with dream about grabbing Oscar

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved around into a new order
a word grabbing something holds it within its grip

blocks.note: and means together with
taken as written, to be rearranged
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film star dreams of winning an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'Oscar' suggest Hollywood, but the stars are in the night sky and Oscar is a phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: New way to leave behind a fast car

indicators.note: the named letter is left behind, dropped from the word

blocks.note: hot means fresh, just out, as in hot news
a road is a way
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A new route lets a driver outpace a speeding car.
explanation.walkthrough: ROAD loses its A to become ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for high speed and acceleration.

clue.text: City of Pakistan I see featured in stories

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears within it

blocks.note: ah is the exclamation of someone who now understands
lore is a body of traditional stories

explanation.surface: Someone notices a Pakistani city appearing in tales they are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Speed control driving round the bend? No

definitions.text: Speed control driving round the bend? No

blocks.clueFragment: Speed control driving round the bend? No
blocks.note: surface reading: someone is told not to brake while cornering

blocks.clueFragment: Speed control driving round the bend? No
blocks.note: setter's reading: driving round the bend means maddening, and the measure, far from maddening the traffic, soothes it

explanation.surface: A driving instructor rejects slowing on a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving round the bend' is the idiom for making someone mad; the 'No' turns it into its opposite, soothing the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic calming is the use of speed bumps and road narrowing to slow vehicles in towns.

clue.text: Ceremony's an austere do

blocks.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
the indefinite article
dour means stern and austere

explanation.surface: A formal ceremony makes for a joyless party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a party but is a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high from the forehead, so a do in the sense of a hairdo.

clue.text: Scrap old copper to burn?

blocks.note: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, a copper coin
to itch is to burn with desire, or to tingle

explanation.surface: Should someone dump old copper or set it on fire?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old copper' is the pre-1971 penny, abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to get rid of it, to discard it.

clue.text: Head stand

blocks.note: first meaning: to lead or manage an organisation
second meaning: to be a candidate in an election

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the yoga headstand; the two words are separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both managing a business and contesting a seat as a candidate.

clue.text: A round of applause?

blocks.note: surface reading: a burst of clapping from an audience
setter's reading: a circuit of the track run by a winner to receive the crowd's acclaim

explanation.surface: An audience bursts into clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor's celebratory circuit of the stadium is a round taken while being cheered.

clue.text: When one tries to get changed in the dark

definitions.text: When one tries to get changed in the dark

indicators.note: letters that get changed are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to dress in a room without light.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: trying to dress in the dark, you learn nothing about how you look.
explanation.definitionFit: None the wiser means no better informed, just as someone dressing unseen ends up knowing no more.

clue.text: Rich family has to rely on working

indicators.note: letters working are being operated on and reworked into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy family is forced to depend on having jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal family, the Windsors, are a famously wealthy dynasty.

clue.text: Modified, round is a square

indicators.note: modified letters have been altered into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A geometric paradox: a circle, once altered, becomes a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' and 'square' suggest shapes; 'square' is an old-fashioned person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur, figuratively, is someone hopelessly out of date, which is what a square is.

clue.text: Not submerged, but half-way to the bottom

definitions.text: Not submerged, but half-way to the bottom

blocks.clueFragment: Not submerged, but half-way to the bottom
blocks.note: surface reading: something sinking that has reached the midpoint of its descent

blocks.clueFragment: Not submerged, but half-way to the bottom
blocks.note: setter's reading: water up to a joint about midway between a wader's backside and feet

explanation.surface: Something not yet underwater is sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' suggests the seabed but is the buttocks: the joint sits roughly halfway down the leg from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in water up to the legs' middle joint means being only partly immersed.

clue.text: Queen's speech a religious commitment?

blocks.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
enunciation is the articulation of speech

explanation.surface: The monarch's annual address is like a sacred vow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's speech' suggests the British monarch's address opening Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Renunciation of worldly goods is a vow taken by monks and nuns, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Vehicle picked up juvenile delinquent

indicators.note: in a down clue, something picked up is lifted, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young offender was collected by a police vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' sounds like an arrest, but it turns LAD upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who wilfully damages property, a kind of delinquent.

clue.text: Old article about new programme

indicators.note: about means around, so these words go round another letter

blocks.note: aged means old
the indefinite article
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dated newspaper piece is about a fresh television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' applies to the old word and the article together, which wrap round the single letter for new.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme or list of items to be dealt with.

clue.text: England fans also helping out

indicators.note: letters put out of place are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporters of the national team are also pitching in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England fans' suggests football supporters; it is people who love England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglophiles are admirers of England and things English.

clue.text: Avoid heading for runway during take-off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter
something happening during an event falls inside it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a take-off is a parody, a skit

explanation.surface: A pilot steers away from the runway while taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' reads as an aircraft leaving the ground but is a satirical imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to go round its edge, avoiding it.

clue.text: In Too Deep lyric

indicators.note: in tells the solver the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Like a song title: a lyric that has got in over its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Get on news with a lady from Italy

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put or get them on
N is short for new or news
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hears the latest about an Italian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' suggests getting along, but it is putting clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna is the Italian word for a woman or lady, used as a title.

clue.text: I drink during lecture in spring

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within its span

blocks.note: to orate is to deliver a speech, to lecture
taken as written
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A student confesses to drinking in a springtime class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a verb, as in springing from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a place is to arise or originate there.

clue.text: Remain outside area with one's contact

indicators.note: a word placed outside others wraps around them

blocks.note: to lie is to remain, as in lie fallow
A is the abbreviation for area
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of the zone together with their contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contact' reads as a noun, a person someone knows, but the answer is a verb meaning to keep in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in touch with others and cooperate.

clue.text: A sucker for power's brainwashing

blocks.note: taken as written
a git is a stupid, contemptible person, a mug
pro means in favour of
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A fool who craves power falls for indoctrination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Git' is British slang for an unpleasant or foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, especially communist, aimed at indoctrinating the public.
